events.title: nginx first public release
events.summary: Igor Sysoev released nginx 0.1.0 on October 4, 2004 — an event-driven web server built to solve the C10K concurrency problem.
events.about: nginx serves static files, reverse-proxies to app servers (Node, Rails, PHP-FPM), and terminates TLS at scale with low memory per connection. It powers CDNs, API gateways, and Kubernetes ingress controllers. Typical setup: nginx on port 443 → upstream Puma or uvicorn workers handling dynamic requests.

narrative.whyChosen: nginx challenged Apache's dominance with async I/O and became the default edge server for high-traffic sites.
narrative.whyImportant: It made reverse-proxying and load balancing routine for every backend team.
narrative.problemSolved: Process-per-connection Apache models struggled past thousands of concurrent clients.
